feedback:
Written before this candidate races, so it states no outcome for it. The evidence is iteration 3 (score 396.3, the best so far): oval finish rate 1.0 at 1.7 s mean with max_error 0.016, but s-bend progress 0.46 and slalom progress 0.09, both ending off track with max_error about 0.062 to 0.064 against the 0.06 m limit. Steering oscillation (0.18 oval, 0.30 s-bend) and RMS error are small, so the robot is pushed outward on bends rather than ringing. Iteration 2 shows that changing sensor width, wheel track, speed and gains together made the oval worse (finish 0.45), so keeping the iteration 3 geometry is correct. This candidate changes only the speed and gain group: base_speed 1.2 to 1.05, kp 5.0 to 5.5, kd 0.8 to 1.0. Lower speed gives more time to correct on alternating bends, and the extra kd should damp the higher kp. The oval time should rise from about 1.7 s to about 2.0 s, which is still within 3 s. Nothing is out of range, and the geometry is unchanged, so the race isolates the control effect. Approve it: it is a valid, well-motivated step from the best design, and the race is needed to learn whether speed or gain is the limit.

After the race, read the results in this order. If oval completion holds at 1.0 and s-bend or slalom progress rises clearly (s-bend above 0.6, slalom above 0.3) with line_loss_events below 1, the speed reduction is the main driver, so try base_speed 0.95 next while keeping kp 5.5 and kd 1.0. If oval completion falls below 1.0 or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.5, kp is too high, so return kp to 5.0 and keep kd 1.0. If the bends still reach max_error near 0.06 at lower speed with few line-loss events, the limit is steering authority rather than speed, so test kp 6.5 with kd 1.2 before touching the sensors.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress rises above 0.6 and slalom above 0.3 with line_loss_events below 1 and oval still completing: keep kp 5.5, kd 1.0, and try base_speed 0.95, because iteration 3 showed the bends fail at speed 1.2 and the oval has ample time margin.

If oval completion falls below 1.0 or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.5 on any track: reduce kp from 5.5 to 5.0 and keep kd 1.0, because iteration 2's kp 5 with kd 0.8 already showed oscillation costs on the oval.

If bends still reach max_error near 0.06 at base_speed 1.05 with line_loss_events of 1 or more: try kp 6.5 with kd 1.2 at the same speed, to test whether steering authority, not speed, limits the s-bend and slalom.
